questions.statement: Segmentation is a trait that first appears in the phylum Annelida and allows animals to have repeated anatomical units.
questions.explanation: The transcript states that segmentation first appears in Annelida and is defined as the repetition of anatomically identical units.

questions.statement: Earthworms have many bristles called ketae, while leeches have none and instead use suckers as their main body adaptation.
questions.explanation: Earthworms (oligochaetes) have few bristles called ketae (hence the name meaning 'few bristles'), and leeches have suckers on both ends but are also described as having synapomorphies distinct from ketae.

questions.statement: The three largest and most diverse animal groups that display segmentation are Annelida, Arthropoda, and Chordata.
questions.explanation: The transcript specifies that Annelida, Arthropoda, and Chordata are the three biggest and most diverse segmented animal groups.

questions.statement: The segmented body of arthropods is always divided into exactly three parts: head, thorax, and abdomen.
questions.explanation: The transcript says arthropod bodies 'in most cases, are broken up into three segments,' implying exceptions exist.

questions.statement: Plesiomorphies are shared derived traits that define a phylum, while synapomorphies are very basic traits shared due to common ancestry.
questions.explanation: According to the transcript, synapomorphies are shared derived traits defining a group, while plesiomorphies are very basic traits shared due to distant common ancestry.
